basic_info.name: NirogStreet Vaidya Tool (now marketed as the Nirog Partner Patient Management System)
basic_info.description: The NirogStreet Vaidya Tool is a SaaS clinic-management product for Ayurvedic practitioners in India, launched in September 2019 by the Delhi-based Ayurveda platform NirogStreet (legal entity Hinirog Healthtech Private Limited). It lets a Vaidya create and manage patient records, patient follow-ups, medicine prescriptions, bills, inventory and medicine stock, and it bundles a curated knowledge layer of 250+ disease treatment protocols, diet and lifestyle guidance, Prakruti Parikshana (constitution assessment) records, Suvarna Prashan records and investigation records. The single most load-bearing fact for this sweep is its current availability: the vendor's website nirogstreet.com returned a literal 'WEBSITE TEMPORARILY UNAVAILABLE' holding page on live fetch on 2026-09-16 (the same condition first observed 2026-09-11), even though the company's Android/iOS apps remain listed and were updated in April 2026 - so the web-delivered Vaidya Tool / Nirog Partner product cannot be confirmed as actively purchasable or reachable today. The product is practitioner-side, cloud/app-based, and is oriented toward consultation plus medicine-order fulfilment rather than toward patient-facing pre-consultation history capture or standards-conformant clinical summary emission. There is no evidence of any NRCeS/ABDM FHIR output, no patient-facing kiosk intake, no voice-based conversational history-taking and no offline-first operation.
basic_info.organization: Hinirog Healthtech Private Limited, trading as NirogStreet; founded 2016 in New Delhi by Ram N Kumar, Shrey Jain and Robin Jha (later co-founders/leaders include Robin Jha and, from 2026, Rishab Malik). Investors include Spiral Ventures, Wavemaker Partners, Jungle Ventures, CE-Ventures/Crescent Enterprises and ICMG.
basic_info.country: India (headquartered New Delhi; reports a presence in the United States and a distributed workforce including Singapore)

technical_features.what_it_does: The Vaidya Tool is a practitioner-facing clinic-management SaaS. On the record-and-prescribe side it supports patient registration and longitudinal patient records, patient follow-up tracking, medicine prescription generation, billing, inventory and medicine stock management, and storage of investigation records. On the knowledge side it ships a curated content layer used at the point of prescribing: treatment protocols for 250+ diseases, diet and lifestyle modification guidance, Prakruti Parikshana (Ayurvedic constitution assessment) records and Suvarna Prashan (a paediatric Rasayana protocol) records. In its current form the product is bundled into the 'Nirog Partner' programme, where a doctor receives appointment leads, views/edits patient information from a consultation (conducted over third-party Google Meet video), places medicine orders on the patient's behalf through the NirogStreet marketplace and earns a margin. It does not generate a physician-ready structured clinical summary, does not emit a FHIR Composition or ABDM artifact, and does not perform automated document digitization into structured clinical resources.
technical_features.architecture: Cloud/hosted multi-tenant SaaS with a web front end and Android (com.app.nirogstreet) and iOS (id1352321621) mobile clients; the company's published tech stack signals Flutter, React and a conventional web stack. Teleconsultation is not native - the published workflow has doctors meeting patients over Google Meet and then logging outcomes in the tool. The system maintains a cloud patient record and a medicine catalogue/marketplace as its two load-bearing data stores.
technical_features.inputs: Practitioner-entered patient demographics and records, consultation notes, prescriptions, investigation records, Prakruti Parikshana and Suvarna Prashan entries, billing and inventory data, and medicine orders placed against the marketplace; appointment leads flow in from the platform.
technical_features.outputs: Digitized patient records, generated prescriptions, bills, inventory/stock reports and medicine order records held as vendor-proprietary data; follow-up status shown in 'My Appointments' and 'Appointment Requests'. No open or standards-based interchange format (no FHIR bundle, no Composition, no national-record push) was found documented.
technical_features.standards_compliance: [uncertain] No evidence was found that the Vaidya Tool claims or implements any formal health-data interoperability standard. Searches found no NRCeS FHIR IG for ABDM conformance, no OPConsultRecord or HealthDocumentRecord emission, no SNOMED CT/LOINC/ICD coding commitment, and no ABDM HIP/HIU role documentation for this product. It is a closed, proprietary clinic-management application rather than a standards-conformant clinical-record system. This should be treated as unverified rather than proven absent.
technical_features.offline_capability: [uncertain] The product is described as cloud/SaaS with web and mobile clients and a marketplace backend, and no offline-first mode, local encrypted store-and-forward queue or LAN deployment is documented. The Android listing states only that data is encrypted in transit. Whether the mobile app caches records for short offline use is not published and could not be verified, especially while the vendor website is down.
technical_features.languages_supported: [uncertain] The practitioner app and marketing content are predominantly English with Sanskrit shloka references in the product copy, signalling an Ayurveda-literate Indian professional audience. No explicit list of supported Indian languages or Devanagari/Hinglish interface support was published for the Vaidya Tool; Hindi/vernacular support cannot be confirmed.
technical_features.deployment_model: Cloud SaaS consumed through a browser and through Android/iOS mobile apps; no kiosk, on-premises, room-server or local-inference deployment is described. Practitioners use their own devices; teleconsultation runs on third-party Google Meet.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: [uncertain] No published accuracy, F1, ROUGE, concept-recall, concordance or clinical error-rate evaluation of the Vaidya Tool was found. The only quality-adjacent claims are operational/marketing (e.g. that the tool reduces record-keeping effort); these are not peer-reviewed and none of them concerns summary or coding quality.
performance_metrics.latency: [uncertain] No published latency, throughput or time-to-note figures were found. Because the clinical record is manually entered by the practitioner after a Google Meet consultation, the product does not perform automated summarization whose latency could be measured.
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: [uncertain] Not published. As a cloud SaaS the inference/processing burden sits server-side and the client is an ordinary browser or phone; no on-device CPU/RAM/GPU footprint is documented.
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: Historical adoption claims from launch and press: 40,000+ Ayurvedic doctors enabled on the NirogStreet application and ~8,000 doctors ordering medicines via the e-commerce platform (2019, vendor/corporate-communication figures); 5.5 lakh (550,000) Ayurveda practitioners targeted to be enabled. More recent third-party estimates: 100K+ Google Play downloads, 2.31K reviews (3.7 stars), ~213 employees (LinkedIn, down ~13.8% year-on-year), and annual revenue around USD 2.2M (LinkedIn estimate) or USD 4.32M for FY2023 (The Company Check). No current active-practitioner count for the Vaidya Tool specifically was found.
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: [uncertain] There is no documented evaluation protocol - no dataset, metric set, judge design or human-review study - for the Vaidya Tool. All available quality statements are vendor/PR claims, so the product's clinical utility is unevaluated in the public literature.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: NirogStreet is the most prominent AYUSH-native practitioner SaaS in India and is therefore the closest existing analogue for where a MediKiosk-generated summary would eventually land: a Vaidya's clinic record system. It matters to Module C in three ways. First, it validates that structured, longitudinal patient records and prescription workflow are commercially wanted by Ayurvedic practitioners in India - the demand side of the summary handoff exists. Second, it defines what Module C must beat: NirogStreet captures records as free, practitioner-typed fields and has no standards-based clinical document, no automated capture, no bilingual structured summary and no national-record push, so a physician-ready NRCeS-conformant summary is genuinely additive rather than competitive with it. Third, its reported trajectory - declining headcount, flat small revenue, no funding since 2023, and a web front door that is currently returning 'WEBSITE TEMPORARILY UNAVAILABLE' - is a caution about the fragility of small AYUSH SaaS vendors and argues for MediKiosk to integrate through open standards rather than depending on any single AYUSH EHR vendor's survival.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (1) the bundled AYUSH knowledge layer - disease protocols plus Prakruti/Suvarna structured records - because it proves AYUSH-specific structured data entry has practitioner pull and maps onto MediKiosk's Dashavidha/Prakriti capture; (2) the free-to-practitioner distribution model for the clinical tool, with monetization moved to medicine logistics, as a realistic AYUSH software business pattern; (3) the practitioner-editable record model, which is consistent with Module C's physician-attestation stance. Reject: (1) free-text, practitioner-typed data entry as the capture mechanism - Module C's value depends on machine-captured, per-field-provenanced structured data; (2) reliance on third-party consumer video (Google Meet) and a marketplace as the clinical substrate; (3) a closed proprietary record store with no FHIR/ABDM export; (4) any design that assumes a stable vendor-hosted web portal, since that is exactly the failure mode currently visible.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: Principal risk finding for this sweep: availability. nirogstreet.com resolves to a holding page reading 'WEBSITE TEMPORARILY UNAVAILABLE / We'll be back soon / Due to some technical issues, our website is currently unavailable' as of a live fetch on 2026-09-16, the same condition reported 2026-09-11 - so the web Vaidya Tool / Nirog Partner product should not be cited as active, and any claim of current users or volumes is unverifiable. The company's own LinkedIn posts add corroborating stress signals: a May 2026 public warning that an unauthorised website is misusing its trademark and doctors' profiles, and an April 2026 leadership change ('Rishab Malik ... driving operations since October 2025'). Headcount has fallen (~213, -13.8% YoY). Product reviews on the Play Store include recent complaints about paid consultations not delivered. There is no evidence of ABDM/FHIR conformance, no offline capability, no patient-facing intake, no document digitization, no summarization, and no published clinical evaluation. Because the vendor site is down, several fields above are marked uncertain rather than confirmed.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: NirogStreet sits on the opposite side of the consultation from MediKiosk and does not erode its differentiation; it exposes a gap. NirogStreet is practitioner-side, web/app, closed-record, English-first, medicine-commerce-centred, with no standards output and no offline story. MediKiosk is patient-facing, offline-first, India-resident, captures voice+touch history before the visit, digitizes physical documents, and emits one bilingual physician-ready summary against the NRCeS FHIR IG OPConsultRecord with per-field provenance and physician attestation. If anything, NirogStreet's current website outage strengthens MediKiosk's argument that AYUSH clinical records should be built on open ABDM standards and local resilience rather than on fragile vendor portals. The one place NirogStreet is ahead is AYUSH domain content (250+ treatment protocols); Module C should treat that as a content-benchmark to match in its rendered output, not as an architectural competitor.

business_info.license: Proprietary commercial SaaS; no open-source license. Brand and software owned by Hinirog Healthtech Private Limited.
business_info.pricing: [uncertain] Historically the Vaidya Tool was offered complementary (free) to Ayurveda practitioners. In its current Nirog Partner form the Patient Management System is described as free to Nirog Partner doctors while carrying a stated value of INR 20,000, with NirogStreet monetizing through medicine orders (doctor margins). Because the vendor website is unavailable, current prices and plan terms could not be confirmed live.
business_info.funding: VC-backed. Reported cumulative funding of roughly USD 24.7-24.8M across about 8 rounds (some aggregators show higher 'raised-to-date' figures). Key rounds: ~USD 2M pre-Series A (Oct 2020, Wavemaker Partners / Amand Ventures), ~USD 2.5M Series A (Jul 2021), ~USD 4M Series A (Dec 2021, CE-Ventures / ICMG), ~USD 12M Series B (Nov 2022, led by Jungle Ventures), and a ~USD 3M Series B / convertible note (Nov 2023, Jungle Ventures). No new round was found after late 2023; a 2024 VCCircle report said the company aimed to triple revenue and raise fresh capital, but no completed round is recorded.
business_info.commercial_status: Commercial, venture-backed private company. Third-party estimates put annual revenue at roughly USD 2.2M (LinkedIn) to USD 4.3M for FY2023 (The Company Check), with a reported FY2023 net loss of about USD 5.8M. No profit reported. Its public web front door is currently down.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: Other AYUSH/Ayurveda practitioner software and platforms - Tracxn lists Sharda Ayurveda Centre, Searchomeo, Vedose, AYUSKAMA, Online Aayarved and Smart Ayush, alongside broader Indian clinic-EMR/telemedicine players (Practo, Eka Care). Within the specific offline + ABDM + pre-consultation-summary space, the relevant comparators are Eka Care (patient-side ABDM PHR and records digitization) and the offline ABDM entrant CureNet rather than NirogStreet. The closest direct conceptual overlap with Module C's AYUSH record is minimal, because NirogStreet does not do automated history capture or standards-based summary emission.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: [uncertain] No ABDM gateway role (HIP/HIU/PHR), Health Locker, HPR/HFR or FHIR integration was found for the Vaidya Tool. Integrations appear limited to the vendor's own marketplace and to third-party consumer video (Google Meet). No hospital-EHR/HIS interoperability is documented.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: NirogStreet operates in the AYUSH software and Ayurveda e-commerce niche, historically working with the Ministry of AYUSH, regulators and research bodies to promote evidence-based Ayurveda. The broader ecosystem is moving decisively toward ABDM/FHIR conformance (ABDM-compliant HMIS guidance, NRCeS profiles, ABHA adoption), which leaves closed, non-FHIR AYUSH tools structurally exposed. The sector also shows consolidation and fragile unit economics: small AYUSH SaaS vendors like NirogStreet have not raised since 2023 and can lose their public web presence. For MediKiosk this is a procurement/standards tailwind (governments and hospitals increasingly require ABDM compliance) coupled with a warning not to rely on any single discontinued AYUSH portal.

history.release_date: The NirogStreet Vaidya Tool launched on ~4 September 2019. NirogStreet itself was founded in 2016.
history.key_milestones: 2016 company founded (Hinirog Healthtech); 2018-2021 early funding rounds (Spiral Ventures, Wavemaker); Sep 2019 Vaidya Tool launched as a specialised SaaS for Ayurvedic practitioners, clinics and hospitals with 250+ disease protocols, Prakruti Parikshana and Suvarna Prashan records; Jul 2021 ~USD 2.5M Series A; Dec 2021 ~USD 4M Series A (CE-Ventures/ICMG); Nov 2022 ~USD 12M Series B led by Jungle Ventures; Nov 2023 ~USD 3M Series B/convertible note; 2024 stated aim to triple revenue; Jun-Jul 2025 'Nirog Partner' digital-clinic and free Patient Management System (valued INR 20,000) launched; Oct 2025 new operational leadership begins; Apr 2026 leadership publicly handed to Rishab Malik and app updated; May 2026 public warning about an impersonating website.
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: Within the last six months (roughly Mar-Sep 2026): the Android app received an update on 15 April 2026 adding volume-based discounts, rewards-to-cart, an appointment/profile revamp and deep-link handling. On 15 April 2026 the app listing iteration added a doctor feedback section and patient-review counts. A 20 April 2026 LinkedIn post announced that Rishab Malik now leads the company with operations driven since October 2025. On 8 May 2026 NirogStreet published a public notice that an unauthorised website was misusing its trademark, branding, content and doctors' profiles, directing users only to nirogstreet.com and official app stores. Around mid-2026 its LinkedIn profile showed ~213 employees, down 13.8% year-on-year, with annual revenue estimated at ~USD 2.2M. Critically, on live fetch on 2026-09-16 the nirogstreet.com home page returned a 'WEBSITE TEMPORARILY UNAVAILABLE' holding page - the same condition first observed 2026-09-11 - so the web product's current operational status is unconfirmed.

market_positioning.target_users: Ayurvedic practitioners (Vaidyas), Ayurveda clinics and hospitals in India, plus Ayurveda students and the wider practitioner community; patients are reached indirectly as the doctors' clients and as medicine buyers on the marketplace.
market_positioning.market_segment: AYUSH / Ayurveda practitioner software - clinic management, EHR-lite records and prescription management, bundled with a B2B2C Ayurvedic medicine marketplace and doctor community.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: NirogStreet positions itself as 'India's No.1 platform for Ayurveda doctors' and 'an ecosystem of Ayurveda' working to make Ayurveda the first call of treatment; the Vaidya Tool / Nirog Partner Patient Management System is pitched as a free, high-value digital clinic that helps a Vaidya manage patient records, generate prescriptions and ship medicines to patients while earning a margin.
